newsitem.title: USA: U.S. budget gap widened in August.
newsitem.headline: U.S. budget gap widened in August.

text.p: The government's budget deficit widened in August to $41.83 billion, a 23.6 percent increase from the $33.85 billion shortfall posted a year earlier in August 1995, the Treasury Department said Monday.
Last month's deficit also was far higher than July's shortfall of $27.1 billion.

One reason cited by the Treasury for the big monthly gap was that pay to military members as well as veterans' benefits and supplemental security income payments that were scheduled for Sept. 1 were accelerated to Aug. 30.
Since Sept. 1 was a Sunday, the checks were mailed out on the preceding Friday to avoid delays to recipients, which had the effect of boosting government spending in August.
Total spending in August was $141.83 billion, an increase from the $130.99 billion of outlays made in July and up from $130.49 billion spent in August 1995.
Income, mainly from taxes, dropped in August to $99.99 billion from $103.89 billion in July but exceeded the $96.64 billion the government took in during August 1995.
Despite the big deficit in August, the government remained well on its way to once more shrinking its red-ink total for the full year.

During the first 11 months of fiscal 1996 that ends on Sept. 30, the budget deficit totalled $143.96 billion. That was down 16 percent from the $171.11 billion total posted in the first 11 months of fisal 1995.
September typically brings a surplus in the monthly budget.
As a result, the Clinton administration is forecasting the deficit for the full 1996 fiscal year will drop to $116.75 billion from fiscal 1995's deficit total of $163.87 billion.
